Using tax operations as an example, she describes an agent assembling W-8IMY documentation for payments to intermediaries, moving fully supported allocations forward, requesting missing paperwork for individual payees and routing conflicts to specialists without making the tax determination itself. She says the real sophistication lies in how clearly the boundaries are drawn between agent orchestration, deterministic regulatory rules and human judgment.
item.dc:creator: Maria Scott

item.title: AI Isn't Replacing Customer Success; It's Rewiring It
item.description: Meza AI CEO Abhishek Yadav cites a Gartner survey in which only 20% of customer service leaders cut staff because of AI, while 55% held headcount steady with higher volumes and 42% were hiring specialized AI roles, as evidence that AI is reshaping customer success rather than replacing it. Drawing on McKinsey's agentic-organization roles, he maps AI-augmented front-line workers to CSMs, T-shaped experts to customer engineers and M-shaped supervisors to CS leaders who manage portfolios of agents. He argues agents give CSMs sharper account insight, while judgment under social pressure stays human, shifting the job toward designing and auditing what agents do.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Yadav

item.title: Your Security AI Needs A Flight Simulator
item.description: SimSpace CTO Lee Rossey uses Capt. Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger's Hudson River landing to argue that, like pilots training in simulators, security teams can't prepare for AI-driven attacks using historical telemetry alone. He cites Anthropic's Mythos preview, which found a 27-year-old OpenBSD vulnerability and chained four flaws into one exploit, as evidence that AI can open attack paths defenders have never seen. Rossey advocates "hyper-synthetic data" generated by re-creating plausible attacks in controlled environments, varying their timing and sequence to train security AI and analysts and expose detection gaps before a real attack.
item.dc:creator: Lee Rossey

item.title: The Cost Of Cutting Corners: Planning Healthcare Cybersecurity And Recovery Around Patient Care
item.description: Visiontech Systems CEO Aliasgar Dohadwala, citing IBM's finding that healthcare breaches cost an average of $6.64 million, urges hospital leaders to plan cybersecurity and recovery spending around one question: what would happen to patient care if a given service went down? He recommends mapping critical clinical workflows and their technology dependencies, checking whether existing controls actually work before buying more, budgeting for the people who respond to alerts, and regularly testing full restoration rather than assuming backups suffice. Downtime procedures should be rehearsed with clinical departments, and any cut to a critical control should spell out which service becomes more exposed and who accepts that risk.
item.dc:creator: Aliasgar Dohadwala

item.title: Why Advertising Is Shifting From Attribution To AI-Based Prediction Models
item.description: SmartyAds consultant Ivan Guzenko argues that click-based attribution is losing its footing as privacy rules and cookie blocking in browsers like Safari and Firefox erode cross-site tracking, citing Mediaocean survey data that marketers trust AI for analysis far more than for campaign decisions. He sees prediction taking over through a revival of marketing mix modeling, incrementality testing and AI models trained inside data clean rooms. Guzenko advises cleaning up data flows between DSPs, CRMs and measurement tools, demanding transparency from vendors, and keeping humans in the loop, warning that an opaque forecast is "just attribution's black box wearing a new label."
item.dc:creator: Ivan Guzenko

item.title: Forward-Deployed Engineering From Within
item.description: Canadian Tire Corp. EVP and CITO Rex Lee notes the rush by Accenture and Microsoft, AWS and Tata Consultancy Services to build forward-deployed engineer teams, but argues that "Vendor FDEs make their products better. Internal FDEs make the enterprise better." He says AI tools make rapid prototypes easy, but ungoverned citizen development risks a sprawl of redundant point solutions, so companies need layered delivery from citizen development to FDE-enabled to fully engineered systems. Internal FDEs embedded with business teams, he writes, keep institutional knowledge in-house and feed reusable patterns back into shared platforms, though the model requires change management, talent investment and clear guardrails.
item.dc:creator: Rex Lee

item.title: Connection Is Not Comprehension: Why AI Agents Need A Unified Semantic Layer
item.description: Denodo senior product director Felix Liao argues that protocols like MCP make it easy to connect AI agents to enterprise data, but "connection is not comprehension": without shared business definitions, agents guess at what fields like revenue mean and act on errors "at machine speed." Wiring agents directly to each source produces inconsistent answers and fragmented governance, he says, while centralizing data in a lakehouse misses sources that can't be moved and lags operational systems. He recommends a unified semantic layer that defines metrics, terms and access policies once across all sources, along with auditing existing definitions and assigning owners to core metrics.
item.dc:creator: Felix Liao

item.title: Will Physical AI Bring A “Coding Agent” To Physical Businesses?
item.description: Palona CEO Maria Zhang argues that restaurants, stores and warehouses could get the equivalent of coding agents, but only with AI models that understand real-world interactions rather than simply describing camera scenes. She says such models need spatial grounding, temporal continuity through occlusion and semantic context to tell, for instance, a customer waiting to order from one passing through, and points to self-supervised approaches like Meta's V-JEPA 2. Noting that live trials affect staff and customers in ways software tests do not ("A codebase can be branched; the lunch rush cannot."), she recommends advancing from recorded-event evaluation and simulation to shadow-mode recommendations before granting agents broader authority.
item.dc:creator: Maria Zhang
